practice: in her artistic practice, natasha works with sculpture, installation, object, video art, and sound, analysing the mechanisms that shape visual statements and the boundaries of the visible.
subject: her research focuses on visual strategies of understatement, practices of veiling, and processes of censoring and concealing information—both in the physical urban environment and in digital space. through a delicate deconstruction of everyday and technological contexts, the artist examines the mechanisms of hiding, distortion, and partial removal of images.
method: her working method is based on field observation and the collection and systematisation of data. working at the intersection of material and audiovisual media, she builds a complex system of traces and gaps, revealing hidden subtexts and invisible structures that shape contemporary perception.
